messages:
tara: Quick check-in: post-launch backlog — we have three small bugs reported + a design polish that would make onboarding <2min. Do we bite the polish now or clear bugs first?
devin: Bugs-first. Tickets are churny in support and block trial conversions.
tara: Agreed, but the polish is a visible win for self-serve. It might improve conversion by a measurable amount.
ravi: Technical note: bug B2 is from a recent scheduler tweak. Fix is ~1 day but needs careful DB migration check.
emily: If B2 has migration risk, could we do B1+B3 now and schedule B2 as hotfix with a short canary? That buys time for polish planning.
tara: Option A: B1+B2+B3 this sprint. Option B: B1+B3 + small canary for B2 (hotfix path). Option C: Skip bugs and deliver polish.
devin: Real-world impact: two trials have been stuck because of B1. That feels urgent.
emily: I can scope a "demoable" polish slice (only the welcome flow + reduced steps) that lands in ~4 dev-days.
tara: Ops-bot: Deploy window reminder: next slot 2024-04-04T02:00Z; emergency hotfixes accepted outside window.
ops-bot: [automated] Please include rollback steps when scheduling hotfixes.
ravi: For B2 migration, hotfix branch + dry-run migration in staging -> canary to 5% traffic -> monitor 6 hours. I'll own rollback playbook.
devin: Sounds safe. Proposal: execute B1+B3 in normal sprint; run B2 as hotfix with canary; put the demoable polish into the following iteration with priority for conversion experiments.
tara: Decision: follow devin's proposal. Owners: devin -> B1+B3, ravi -> B2 hotfix canary, emily -> polish spec for next sprint.
emily: I'll post the minimal spec and sample screens in #design by EOD.
ravi: I'll schedule the staging migration dry-run tonight and ping for canary approval.
tara: I'll update the roadmap and notify the two affected trials of expected ETA for fixes. Closing after PRs linked.
ops-bot: [automated] Canary approval required 2 hours before deploy window.
tara: Thanks all, good tradeoff.
